description: Use case: the main results of a rooftop photovoltaic installation in Switzerland over its lifetime, the electricity produced and the CO2-eq saved against the Swiss consumption mix and against a replacement mix, as shown on the page 'PV lifetime CO2 balance'. The inputs are the system size in kWp, the orientation as a yield factor, the usable battery capacity and the annual household consumption; the worked example is 10 kWp east-west, 10 kWh battery, 4500 kWh. Every delivered kWh, used at home or exported, is assumed to displace one kWh of the reference mix; the embodied emission of the PV system (IEA PVPS 2023 reference, converted to a fixed amount per kWp) and of the batteries bought over the lifetime is subtracted. The CO2-eq saving is stated three times: with the annual Swiss consumption mix of 2018 (KBOB), with the monthly Swiss consumption mix 2018 to 2022 (treeze) weighted by the PV electricity delivered in each month, which is lower because PV produces in summer when the Swiss mix is cleanest, and with the European residual mix (Swissolar) as the replacement mix. The monthly dispatch of the page (direct use capped by the day share of the consumption, battery charge capped by one cycle a day and the night consumption) needs a minimum function, so its two annual sums and the PV-weighted mix are stored as modelled values; all other results are formulas of the file and reproduced by the calc-validation. The inputs that are not measured carry the word assumed and a confidence.

words.name: electricity
words.description: energy from the flow of electric charge

words.name: mix
words.description: the combination of generation technologies behind one kWh of electricity, weighted by their share

words.name: production
words.description: the making of a good or an energy, here the electricity generated within a country

words.name: residual
words.description: what remains after the tracked part is taken out; for electricity the mix that is left after all guarantees of origin have been assigned

words.name: avoided
words.description: not caused, because something else has taken its place

words.name: CO2-eq
words.description: carbon dioxide equivalent: the amount of CO2 with the same global warming effect as the mix of climate gases released

words.name: lifetime
words.description: the years a system is operated before it is dismantled

words.name: embodied
words.description: built into a product during its making, for an emission the greenhouse gases released by the production, transport and disposal of the product

words.name: payback
words.description: the time until the saving has repaid the initial cost; for emissions the operating years until the avoided emission equals the embodied emission

words.name: kWp
words.description: kilowatt peak: the rated power of a PV system under standard test conditions

words.name: battery
words.description: an electrochemical store; here a stationary lithium-ion home storage system charged by the PV surplus

words.name: delivered
words.description: handed to a consumer, at home or through the grid

words.name: autarky
words.description: the share of the own consumption that is covered by the own production

words.name: day
words.description: here the hours with PV production

triples.description: photovoltaic electricity generated in Switzerland, the subject of this use case; the table of this phrase compares its climate benefit with and without the displacement concept

triples.name: PV installation
triples.description: a photovoltaic system on a building: the modules, the inverter and, if present, the battery

triples.name: example PV installation
triples.description: the default installation of the page: 10 kWp east-west on a flat roof in the Swiss plateau, a 10 kWh battery and a household that uses 4500 kWh a year; every input can be changed, the numbers of this phrase are the worked example

triples.name: consumption mix
triples.description: the average mix of the electricity consumed in a country including the imports; the reference of the classic comparison without the displacement concept

triples.name: production mix
triples.description: the average mix of the electricity generated within a country, without imports and exports

triples.name: residual mix
triples.description: the European mix that remains after all guarantees of origin have been taken out, so the generation a consumer without a certificate gets; used on the page as the replacement mix, the second reference next to the Swiss consumption mix

triples.name: PV-weighted consumption mix
triples.description: the Swiss consumption mix averaged over the twelve months with the PV electricity delivered in each month as the weight; lower than the annual mean, because PV produces most in summer when the Swiss mix is cleanest

triples.name: life cycle
triples.description: the whole life of a product from the raw materials over the use to the disposal, the scope of a life cycle assessment

triples.name: embodied emission
triples.description: the greenhouse gases released to make, install and dispose of a system, before it has delivered any electricity

triples.name: embodied intensity
triples.description: the embodied emission per unit of rated power

triples.name: PV embodied intensity
triples.description: the embodied emission of one kWp of PV, derived from the life cycle emission per kWh of the reference system times its reference yield and lifetime

triples.name: avoided emission
triples.description: the emission of the reference mix minus the emission of the new source, so the climate benefit of one kWh of the new source

triples.name: gross avoided emission
triples.description: the emission of the reference mix that the delivered PV electricity displaces, before the embodied emission of the installation is subtracted

triples.name: net avoided emission
triples.description: the gross avoided emission minus the embodied emission of the PV system and the battery: the lifetime climate benefit of the installation

triples.name: emission payback
triples.description: the years of operation until the avoided emission has repaid the embodied emission
the unit of the emission intensity of electricity
the unit of the production emission of a battery per kWh of storage capacity
the unit of the embodied emission of a PV system per kWp of rated power

triples.name: yield factor
triples.description: the annual yield of a panel orientation relative to the best orientation, south with 30 degree tilt

triples.name: east-west
triples.description: half the modules facing east, half facing west, the usual layout on a flat roof

triples.name: PV capacity
triples.description: the rated power of the PV modules in kWp

triples.name: PV production
triples.description: the electricity the PV modules generate

triples.name: lifetime production
triples.description: the PV production summed over the lifetime of the installation

triples.name: battery capacity
triples.description: the usable storage capacity of the battery in kWh

triples.name: battery charge
triples.description: the PV surplus that goes into the battery

triples.name: battery discharge
triples.description: the electricity the battery gives back to the house, the charge minus the losses

triples.name: round-trip efficiency
triples.description: the share of the charged energy that comes back out of the battery

triples.name: battery count
triples.description: how many batteries are bought over the lifetime of the installation, the lifetime divided by the battery lifetime rounded up

triples.name: battery production emission
triples.description: the greenhouse gases released to produce one kWh of battery storage capacity

triples.name: household consumption
triples.description: the electricity the household uses in a year, the local consumption that the PV electricity can replace first

triples.name: direct use
triples.description: the PV electricity used in the house in the hour it is produced

triples.name: grid import
triples.description: the electricity the household still buys from the grid

triples.name: delivered electricity
triples.description: the PV electricity that reaches a consumer: used directly, taken from the battery after the losses, or exported; every delivered kWh is assumed to displace one kWh of the reference mix

triples.name: self-consumption share
triples.description: the share of the PV production that is used on site, directly or via the battery

triples.name: day share
triples.description: the share of the household consumption that falls into the hours with PV production

triples.name: monthly share
triples.description: the share of an annual amount that falls into one month

formulas.name: PV production by orientation
formulas.description: the annual PV production: the rated power times the specific yield of the best orientation times the yield factor of the real orientation

formulas.name: lifetime production formula
formulas.description: the PV production over the whole lifetime; the degradation of the modules is already part of the lifetime average yield

formulas.name: battery discharge formula
formulas.description: what the battery gives back: the charge times the round-trip efficiency

formulas.name: export formula
formulas.description: the PV production that is neither used directly nor stored goes to the grid

formulas.name: grid import formula
formulas.description: the consumption not covered by direct use and battery discharge is bought from the grid

formulas.name: delivered electricity formula
formulas.description: the PV electricity that reaches a consumer, so the production minus the battery losses

formulas.name: self-consumption share by dispatch
formulas.description: the share of the production used on site; the battery charge counts in full, because the losses happen on site too

formulas.name: autarky formula
formulas.description: the share of the household consumption covered by the own PV electricity

formulas.name: PV embodied intensity formula
formulas.description: turns the life cycle emission per kWh of the reference system into a fixed amount per kWp: the emission per kWh is spread over the reference yield and lifetime, so a site with a lower yield has the same embodied emission and a higher emission per kWh; the division by 1000 converts gram to kg

formulas.name: battery embodied emission formula
formulas.description: the production emission of all batteries bought over the lifetime
formulas.expression: "battery embodied emission" = "battery capacity" * "battery production emission" * "battery count"

formulas.name: gross avoided emission by consumption mix
formulas.description: the emission of the Swiss consumption mix that the delivered PV electricity displaces over the lifetime; one formula per reference mix, because the mix is the operand; the division by 1000 converts gram to kg

formulas.name: gross avoided emission by PV-weighted consumption mix
formulas.description: the same with the Swiss consumption mix weighted by the monthly PV delivery
formulas.expression: "gross avoided emission" = "lifetime delivered electricity" * "PV-weighted consumption mix" / 1000

formulas.name: gross avoided emission by residual mix
formulas.description: the same with the European residual mix as the replacement mix

formulas.name: net avoided emission formula
formulas.description: the gross avoided emission minus the embodied emission of the PV system and the battery; the reference mix is selected by the context
formulas.expression: "net avoided emission" = "gross avoided emission" - "PV embodied emission" - "battery embodied emission"

formulas.name: emission payback formula
formulas.description: the operating years until the gross avoided emission equals the embodied emission, assuming an even avoided emission per year
formulas.expression: "emission payback" = ( "PV embodied emission" + "battery embodied emission" ) / "gross avoided emission" * "lifetime"

sources.name: IEA PVPS Task 12 fact sheet 2023
sources.description: Stucki M., Götz M., de Wild-Scholten M., Frischknecht R.: Ökobilanz von Strom aus PV-Anlagen, Aktualisierung der Daten für das Jahr 2023. IEA PVPS Task 12 fact sheet, 2024. Reference system: 3 kWp mono-crystalline pitched roof system in Switzerland, 976 kWh/kWp annual yield including a linear degradation of 0.7 percent per year, 30 years lifetime, 35.8 g CO2-eq per kWh AC (modules 20.2, inverter 9.9, rest 5.8).

sources.name: KBOB energy systems 2022
sources.description: Ramseier L., Frischknecht R. (treeze Ltd.): Umweltkennwerte und Primärenergiefaktoren von Energiesystemen, UVEK Ökobilanzdatenbestand DQRv2:2022, for KBOB, BAFU and AHB, Uster, 9 March 2022. Table 'Elektrizität, Bezug via Netz' gives the greenhouse gas emissions per MJ of electricity for the Swiss mixes of 2018 (CH-Verbrauchermix 0.035, CH-Produktionsmix 0.009, CH-Lieferantenmix HKN 0.015 kg CO2-eq/MJ) and for photovoltaic electricity (Fotovoltaik 0.013 kg CO2-eq/MJ); the mixes are documented in Krebs & Frischknecht (2020) and Frischknecht et al. (2020), Umweltbilanz Strommixe Schweiz 2018, BAFU.

sources.name: treeze monthly electricity mixes 2025
sources.description: Frischknecht R. (treeze Ltd.): Ökobilanz der monatlichen Strombereitstellung Schweiz und Europa, for the Amt für Hochbauten der Stadt Zürich, Uster, 4 June 2025. Table 5.1: monthly greenhouse gas emissions of the Swiss consumer mix at low voltage 2018 to 2022 and the mean of the five years; chapter 6: the monthly European production mix 2022 varies between about 350 (May) and 440 (September) g CO2-eq per kWh.

sources.name: Swissolar PV fact sheet 2024
sources.description: Swissolar: Fiche d'information Photovoltaïque, édition février 2024. Footnote 2 names the reference mixes of the CO2 saving: Swiss consumer mix 128 g CO2-eq per kWh and European residual mix 523 g CO2-eq per kWh, after treeze, Ökobilanz Strom aus Photovoltaikanlagen, Factsheet 1.0, Update 2020.

sources.name: Lithium-ion cell LCA comparison 2025
sources.description: Comparative life cycle assessment of lithium-ion, sodium-ion, and solid-state battery cells for electric vehicles. Journal of Industrial Ecology 29(1):113-128, 2025. Cradle-to-gate production of lithium-ion cells emits about 58 to 92 kg CO2-eq per kWh of cell capacity, optimised LFP cells about 37 kg; the figure covers the cells only, not the housing, inverter and control of a home storage system.

sources.name: HTW Berlin solar storage climate 2019
sources.description: Weniger J., Orth N., Böhme N., Quaschning V. (HTW Berlin): Sind Solarstromspeicher Klimaschützer? 2019. Uses 212 kg CO2-eq per kWh of battery capacity for the production of a lithium home storage system, the upper end of the literature.

sources.name: gruenes.haus tilt and orientation table
sources.description: Janßen K.: Photovoltaik-Neigungswinkel: Tabelle und optimale Dachneigung. gruenes.haus. Annual yield relative to south with 30 degree tilt at 30 degree tilt: south 100, south-east or south-west 95, east or west 82, north 59 percent; flat roof without tilt about 88, east-west with flat tilt about 85 percent. A German installer table, so the figures are indicative for the Swiss plateau.

values.description: the system size, the first input of the page; 10 kWp is a typical single family roof
the usable battery capacity, the third input of the page; set it to 0 for an installation without battery
the local electricity consumption, the fourth input of the page; 4500 kWh is a typical Swiss family household without heat pump or electric car
the best case, the reference of the factor
30 degree tilt facing south-east
30 degree tilt facing south-west
30 degree tilt facing east
30 degree tilt facing west
30 degree tilt facing north
flat roof without tilt
half east, half west with a flat tilt of 10 to 15 degree, the usual flat roof layout; the orientation of the example installation, the second input of the page
the lifetime average annual yield of the reference system, a pitched roof facing south in Switzerland, including the linear degradation of 0.7 percent per year
the reference lifetime of the life cycle assessment

life cycle emission of one kWh AC from a 3 kWp mono-crystalline pitched roof system in Switzerland with the module technology of 2023; the 2018 figure of KBOB is 46.8, see the use case PV in Switzerland

the average Swiss consumption mix of 2018 incl. the imports per hour (table Elektrizität, Bezug via Netz, CH-Verbrauchermix: 0.035 kg CO2-eq/MJ times 3.6 MJ per kWh); exact to about 2 g per kWh, the BAFU report gives 128.0 before the rounding per MJ
the European residual mix that Swissolar uses as the replacement mix for the CO2 saving of PV; the European production mix 2022 of treeze is lower, 350 to 440 g per month
monthly mean of the five years 2018 to 2022 at low voltage, table 5.1; the twelve values are the base of the PV-weighted consumption mix
the share of the household consumption that falls into the hours with PV production; a household where nobody is at home during the day, higher with home office or a heat pump running at noon
a rough split, the hourly profile of a household is well known but varies a lot between households
the usual system efficiency of a lithium-ion home storage incl. the inverter losses
manufacturers state 90 to 95 percent for the cells, measured systems reach 80 to 92 percent
the middle of the literature: cells alone 37 to 92 kg per kWh, a complete home storage system in the HTW study 212 kg per kWh
the published figures span a factor of five, so the middle is a guess
a lithium-ion home storage with one cycle a day lasts 10 to 20 years
the lifetime of 30 years divided by the battery lifetime of 15 years, rounded up: the first battery and one replacement
the share of the annual PV production that falls into the month, a typical profile for the Swiss plateau with winter fog; the twelve shares sum to 1
the seasonal shape is well known from PVGIS, the exact shares depend on the place and the year
the share of the annual household consumption that falls into the month, more in winter for light and heating pumps; the twelve shares sum to 1

monthly dispatch of the page: in each month the direct use is the smaller of the PV production and the day share of the consumption, the battery charge is the smallest of the surplus, one full battery cycle per day and the night consumption divided by the round-trip efficiency; this needs a minimum function that the zukunft.com formulas do not have, so the annual sum is stored as a modelled value
the annual sum of the monthly battery charge of the dispatch described at the direct use

the sum over the twelve months of the delivered PV electricity times the monthly Swiss consumption mix, divided by the annual delivered electricity; a weighted mean of the twelve monthly values above with the monthly dispatch of the page as the weight
